{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_1494670fe15941588a5c97a1","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Deliver a user's conversation list over the WebSocket protocol\n2\t\n3\tIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#144\n4\tLabels: type:feature, size:M, area:api, area:compliance, epic:extension-points\n5\t\n6\tPart of #35\n7\t\n8\t## Why\n9\t\n10\t#143 gives a consumer `store.listFor(userId)`.\n11\tIt does not give a **client** anything: the browser holding the socket cannot reach the store, so\n12\tevery consumer that wants a history sidebar has to stand up its own authenticated HTTP route over\n13\tthe same data the engine already authenticated on the upgrade. That is a second authorisation\n14\tpath to the same personal data, written once per consumer, each one able to get the ownership\n15\tcheck wrong in its own way — the exact failure #45 went out of its way to avoid for resume.\n16\t\n17\tA consumer may have no such route to extend: an engine deployment behind an api with a session\n18\tstore and no conversation endpoints of its own has nothing to add this to. The engine already knows who is connected and already\n19\treplays a conversation on resume; answering \"which conversations do I have\" over the same socket\n20\tis the smaller surface.\n21\t\n22\t## What to do\n23\t\n24\t- `src/types/messages.ts`, additive only:\n25\t  - `ListConversationsMessage {type: 'list_conversations'; limit?: number; before?: string}` into\n26\t    `IncomingMessage`. There is no user id field, and that is the point: the list is always the\n27\t    connection's authenticated user's.\n28\t  - `ConversationListMessage {type: 'conversation_list'; conversations: ConversationSummary[]}`\n29\t    into `OutgoingMessage`, where `ConversationSummary` is `SessionSummary` with its two times as\n30\t    ISO strings — `Date` does not survive `JSON.stringify` as a `Date`, and the protocol types\n31\t    describe what goes on the wire.\n32\t- `validation.ts`: a `list_conversations` case — `limit`, when present, an integer 1–200;\n33\t  `before`, when present, a string `Date.parse` accepts. Anything else is `INVALID_MESSAGE`, as\n34\t  the two existing cases do it.\n35\t- Handling: `createMessageHandler` takes the session store and the new options alongside the\n36\t  orchestrator (`createServer` already holds both), and answers `list_conversations` on the\n37\t  non-locked path beside `ping` — a history request is not a turn and must not queue behind a\n38\t  streaming answer.\n39\t- The user id comes from `ws.userId`, never from the frame. Add the regression:\n40\t  a frame carrying an extra `userId` of another user is answered with the connecting user's own\n41\t  list.\n42\t- Opt-in: `HalEngineConfig.transport.history?: {enabled: boolean}`, default off, threaded through\n43\t  `createServer`'s options like `resume`. With it off, `list_conversations` is answered with an\n44\t  `error` frame and no list.\n45\t- A store that implements no `listFor` is answered with an `error`, not an empty list: a client\n46\t  that renders \"no conversations\" for a user who has several is a worse answer than one that\n47\t  renders a failure. `ErrorCodes` gains one code for both cases (`UNSUPPORTED`), additive.\n48\t- Picking a conversation needs nothing new: the client reconnects with `?sessionId=<id>`, which\n49\t  #45 already ships with the ownership check and the replay. No in-band switch frame, no second\n50\t  replay path.\n51\t- Specs and docs: extend `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md` (the two frames, their\n52\t  field tables, the authorisation rule) and the conversation-list spec; add § Conversation list\n53\t  to `docs/getting-started.md` by editing `example/full-config.ts` and running `npm run docs:fix`\n54\t  — that listing sits under `<!-- doc-block: example/full-config.ts#full-config -->` and\n55\t  `npm run docs:check` fails a hand-edited block.\n56\t\n57\t## Decisions\n58\t\n59\t- **A frame, not a REST route.** The REST chat routes are demo-only and are not where a consumer is meant to build. The WebSocket is where the caller is\n60\t  already authenticated, once per connection, by the consumer's own `wsAuth`.\n61\t- **Its own opt-in flag, separate from `resume`.** Resume hands a client back a conversation it\n62\t  was already in; a list tells it what else the user has. A deployer who turned on resume did not\n63\t  thereby agree to the second disclosure, and a config that conflates them cannot be audited.\n64\t- **Answered off the per-session lock.** `PerSessionLock` serialises turns (#47). A list request\n65\t  that queued behind a two-minute streaming answer would look broken, and it mutates nothing.\n66\t- **An error, not an empty list, when it cannot be answered.** See above; silence that looks like\n67\t  data is the one failure mode a history view cannot recover from.\n68\t- **Answered when asked, never pushed.** No `conversation_list` arrives unsolicited: a client\n69\t  that just started a conversation knows, and a push would need a fan-out across the sockets a\n70\t  resumed session can be open on.\n71\t- **The frame is accepted by `validateMessage` whether or not the feature is on**, and the\n72\t  handler is what refuses it. This was written before\n92\t      #143's review found that paging on a timestamp alone drops a conversation whenever two\n93\t      share an activity time, so the store's cursor became a composite that accepts an ISO\n94\t      string; a `Date` cannot carry the tie-break. Built as originally written, the transport would have reintroduced the defect the store\n137\t   had just been fixed for.\n138\t2. **`messages.ts` gains four interfaces, not two** — the two frames plus the two payload types\n139\t   they describe.\n140\t3. **`StoreCannotList` is new public surface**, beyond what this issue specified: without it a\n141\t   permanent store misconfiguration cannot be told from a transient failure, in either the client\n142\t   frame or the log.\n143\t\n144\tTwo decisions the criteria did not anticipate:\n145\t\n146\t- **`transport.history` without `transport.resume` is useless, and now says so.** `?sessionId=` is\n147\t  read only when resume is enabled, so a list whose rows cannot be opened is a deployment slip:\n148\t  the engine warns at startup and the documentation says so where it tells a client to reconnect\n149\t  with a row's id. no migration guide is owed\n- [ ] `npm run verify` passes and the coverage floors for the touched groups hold or rise\n\n## Amendments\n\nThree things changed between writing this issue and building it, each marked in the criterion it\naffects:\n\n1. **`before` is a cursor, not a timestamp.** #143's review found that paging on `updatedAt` alone\n   silently drops a conversation when two share an activity time. The store's cursor became\n   `{updatedAt, sessionId}`, so the frame carries both halves and the validator refuses one half\n   alone. Built as originally written, the transport would have reintroduced the defect the store\n   had just been fixed for.\n2. **`messages.ts` gains four interfaces, not two** — the two frames plus the two payload types\n   they describe.\n3. **`StoreCannotList` is new public surface**, beyond what this issue specified: without it a\n   permanent store misconfiguration cannot be told from a transient failure, in either the client\n   frame or the log.\n\nTwo decisions the criteria did not anticipate:\n\n- **`transport.history` without `transport.resume` is useless, and now says so.** `?sessionId=` is\n  read only when resume is enabled, so a list whose rows cannot be opened is a deployment slip:\n  the engine warns at startup and the documentation says so where it tells a client to reconnect\n  with a row's id. Refusing to start was considered and rejected as too blunt for a library.\n- **The conversation the connection is in is listed like any other**, so a fresh connect sees a row\n  of its own holding no entries. Filtering it out was rejected: it is a real conversation the user\n  is in, and it is their newest the moment they send anything.\n\n## Tech notes\n\nDepends on #143: without `listFor` there is\nnothing to send.\n\nKey paths: `src/types/messages.ts`, `src/types/session.ts` (`ErrorCodes`),\n`src/transport/ws/{validation,messageHandler,sender}.ts`, `src/transport/createServer.ts`,\n`src/config.ts`, `example/full-config.ts`, `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md`.\n\nOut of scope: a preview or title on the summaries (its own issue); deleting a conversation from\nthe client, which would put an erasure primitive on the wire and needs its own authorisation\ndecision; paging state held server-side — the client pages with `before`; an operator view of\nanother user's conversations, which is an authorisation question of its own; and live sync between open tabs,\nwhich #124 ruled out.\n\nRefs #143, #145, #41, #45, #47, #124\n\n\n\n\n","numLines":174,"startLine":1,"totalLines":174}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_1494670fe15941588a5c97a1","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_c7316914988c4c2ba04b91ae","type":"tool_result","content":"// Command lore-code-trace is the portable CI ingestion orchestrator. With no\n// subcommand it reads a repo's .lore/test-commands.yml, runs the list + per-file\n// run commands, and (with --post) sends the report to Lore; it is a faithful\n// port of the TS buildTestReport/run-tests CLI so any onboarded repo runs one\n// blessed binary instead of drifting inlined bash. `docs` sends the repo's\n// changed specs and ADRs instead (docs_run.go).\npackage main\n\nimport (\n\t\"context\"\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"io\"\n\t\"net/http\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"path/filepath\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"time\"\n)\n\n// Each chunk is POSTed separately, and every POST becomes one event, one\n// assembly run and one Kubernetes pod. At 512 KB this repo's suite packed into\n// 72 chunks per push to main — 72 pods and ~2,500 pod-hours a month to deliver\n// a report that fits comfortably in a single request. The Floor's ingress\n// accepts 25 MB bodies, so 4 MB keeps a wide margin (and stays a reasonable\n// jsonb event payload) while cutting the fan-out roughly eight-fold.\n//\n// This is the cheap lever, not the destination: the incremental sink added in\n// #1742 (POST /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/ingest, after a GET of the repo's\n// ingest-state) projects in-process with no event, no pod and no clone. Its\n// client side was never wired up; until it is, this constant bounds the cost.\nconst (\n\tmanifestRelPath = \".lore/test-commands.yml\"\n\tmaxChunkBytes   = 4_000_000\n\trunConcurrency  = 4\n)\n\n// invocation is the command line, read once: `docs` ingests specs and ADRs,\n// `links` checks their test links, and no subcommand runs the tests and ingests\n// their report.\ntype invocation struct {\n\tdocs  bool\n\tlinks bool\n\tpost  bool\n\tforce bool\n\tall   bool\n\tbase  string\n}\n\nfunc parseArgs(args []string) (invocation, error) {\n\tparsed := invocation{}\n\tfor i := 0; i < len(args); i++ {\n\t\tswitch args[i] {\n\t\tcase \"docs\":\n\t\t\tparsed.docs = true\n\t\tcase \"links\":\n\t\t\tparsed.links = true\n\t\tcase \"--post\":\n\t\t\tparsed.post = true\n\t\tcase \"--force\":\n\t\t\tparsed.force = true\n\t\tcase \"--all\":\n\t\t\tparsed.all = true\n\t\tcase \"--base\":\n\t\t\tif i+1 == len(args) {\n\t\t\t\treturn invocation{}, fmt.Errorf(\"--base needs the name of the branch the change targets\")\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\ti++\n\t\t\tparsed.base = args[i]\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn parsed, nil\n}\n\nfunc main() {\n\twd, err := os.Getwd()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tfmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, \"lore-code-trace:\", err)\n\t\tos.Exit(exitCode(err))\nShell cwd was reset to /private/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/cd97a8e87adc/workspace","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"201e0564-2c41-4a6d-8255-873a75985435","uuid":"f0cef061-bd83-4640-aaaf-aeaecc33b567","timestamp":"2026-10-30T20:42:17.195Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"// Command lore-code-trace is the portable CI ingestion orchestrator. At 512 KB this repo's suite packed into\n// 72 chunks per push to main — 72 pods and ~2,500 pod-hours a month to deliver\n// a report that fits comfortably in a single request. Its\n// client side was never wired up; until it is, this constant bounds the cost.\nconst (\n\tmanifestRelPath = \".lore/test-commands.yml\"\n\tmaxChunkBytes   = 4_000_000\n\trunConcurrency  = 4\n)\n\n// invocation is the command line, read once: `docs` ingests specs and ADRs,\n// `links` checks their test links, and no subcommand runs the tests and ingests\n// their report.\ntype invocation struct {\n\tdocs  bool\n\tlinks bool\n\tpost  bool\n\tforce bool\n\tall   bool\n\tbase  string\n}\n\nfunc parseArgs(args []string) (invocation, error) {\n\tparsed := invocation{}\n\tfor i := 0; i < len(args); i++ {\n\t\tswitch args[i] {\n\t\tcase \"docs\":\n\t\t\tparsed.docs = true\n\t\tcase \"links\":\n\t\t\tparsed.links = true\n\t\tcase \"--post\":\n\t\t\tparsed.post = true\n\t\tcase \"--force\":\n\t\t\tparsed.force = true\n\t\tcase \"--all\":\n\t\t\tparsed.all = true\n\t\tcase \"--base\":\n\t\t\tif i+1 == len(args) {\n\t\t\t\treturn invocation{}, fmt.Errorf(\"--base needs the name of the branch the change targets\")\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\ti++\n\t\t\tparsed.base = args[i]\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn parsed, nil\n}\n\nfunc main() {\n\twd, err := os.Getwd()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tfmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, \"lore-code-trace:\", err)\n\t\tos.Exit(exitCode(err))","stderr":"\nShell cwd was reset to /private/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/cd97a8e87adc/workspace","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_c7316914988c4c2ba04b91ae","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{once} from 'node:events';\nimport type {AddressInfo} from 'node:net';\nimport {WebSocket} from 'ws';\nimport type {Express} from 'express';\nimport {createServer} from './createServer.js';\nimport {HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL} from './ws/subprotocol.js';\nimport type {SessionResumeOptions} from './ws/sessionResume.js';\nimport {answeringOrchestrator} from './wsTestSupport.js';\nimport {InMemorySessionStore} from '../infrastructure/stores/inMemorySessionStore.js';\nimport type {ChatOrchestrator} from '../orchestration/chatOrchestrator.js';\nimport type {MessageChunk} from '../types/ai.js';\nimport type {ConnectedMessage} from '../types/messages.js';\nimport type {SessionEntry} from '../types/session.js';\nimport type {SessionStore} from '../types/sessionStore.js';\nimport {setLogger} from '../shared/logger.js';\n\n// Real upgrades over a real socket: what a reconnect is sent is the contract, and no double can observe it.\n\ninterface Frame {\n  type: string;\n  sessionId?: string;\n  resumed?: boolean;\n  entryCount?: number;\n  resumeFailure?: string;\n  index?: number;\n  entry?: SessionEntry;\n}\n\nconst NEVER_ISSUED = '0f1e2d3c-4b5a-4968-8776-655443322110';\nconst RESUME_ON: SessionResumeOptions = {enabled: true};\nconst LATEST_ON: SessionResumeOptions = {enabled: true, latest: true};\nconst HALF_ANSWER: SessionEntry = {\n  role: 'assistant',\n  content: 'half',\n  timestamp: '2026-09-30T08:00:01.000Z',\n  isStreaming: true,\n};\n\n// A tool's suppression lands while the answer is still open, as when a provider ends a tool round with no stop.\nconst suppressingMidAnswer: ChatOrchestrator = {\n  processMessage: async () => 'before after',\n  async *processMessageStream(): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n    yield {type: 'text', text: 'before'};\n    yield {type: 'suppress_output'} as unknown as MessageChunk;\n    yield {type: 'text', text: ' after'};\n    yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\n  },\n};\n\nconst servers: Array<ReturnType<typeof createServer>> = [];\nconst clients: WebSocket[] = [];\n\nconst eventually = async (check: () => boolean): Promise<void> => {\n  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 50 && !check(); attempt++) await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 10));\n};\n\n// Silenced for the whole file: the server logs every connection and close, and these tests read frames, not logs.\nbeforeAll(() => {\n  setLogger({debug: () => undefined, info: () => undefined, warn: () => undefined, error: () => undefined});\n});\n\nafterAll(() => {\n  setLogger();\n});\n\n// Each server sees its sockets close before it stops, so no close is logged after the logger above is restored.\nafterEach(async () => {\n  for (const client of clients.splice(0)) client.terminate();\n  for (const hal of servers.splice(0)) {\n    const {wss} = hal;\n    await eventually(() => wss.clients.size === 0);\n    await hal.stop();\n  }\n});\n\n// The authenticated user is read per upgrade, so one test can reconnect as someone else.\nconst startEngine = async (\n  store: SessionStore,\n  resume?: SessionResumeOptions,\n  orchestrator: ChatOrchestrator = answeringOrchestrator\n) => {\n  const auth = {userId: 'u1'};\n  const connects: Array<{sessionId: string; resumed: boolean}> = [];\n  const disconnected: string[] = [];\n  const hal = createServer({\n    app: (() => undefined) as unknown as Express,\n    wsAuth: async () => ({id: auth.userId}),\n    sessionStore: store,\n    orchestrator,\n    resume,\n    onConnect: (session, {resumed}) => void connects.push({sessionId: session.sessionId, resumed}),\n    onDisconnect: sessionId => void disconnected.push(sessionId),\n  });\n  // Resolves once the server itself has seen its first socket close, which the client's own close can precede.\n  const firstServerClose = new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    hal.wss.once('connection', socket => socket.once('close', () => resolve()));\n  });\n  await hal.start(0);\n  servers.push(hal);\n  const {port} = hal.server.address() as AddressInfo;\n  return {auth, connects, disconnected, firstServerClose, base: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/hal/ws`};\n};\n\nconst open = (url: string, token = 't'): WebSocket => {\n  const client = new WebSocket(url, [HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL, token]);\n  clients.push(client);\n  return client;\n};\n\n// One question answered and the socket closed, returning the id the connected frame announced.\nconst firstTurn = async (base: string): Promise<string> => {\n  const client = open(base);\n  let sessionId = '';\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') sessionId = frame.sessionId ?? '';\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'user_message', content: 'hello'}));\n      if (frame.type === 'stream_end') resolve();\n    });\n  });\n  client.close();\n  await once(client, 'close');\n  return sessionId;\n};\n\n// A ping sent on connect is a barrier: its pong can only follow every frame the replay wrote.\nconst connectAndSettle = async (url: string, token?: string): Promise<Frame[]> => {\n  const client = open(url, token);\n  const frames: Frame[] = [];\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      frames.push(frame);\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1}));\n      if (frame.type === 'pong') resolve();\n    });\n  });\n  return frames;\n};\n\nconst upserts = (frames: Frame[]) =>\n  frames.filter(frame => frame.type === 'entry_upsert').map(({index, entry}) => ({index, entry}));\n\nconst shapeOf = (frames: Frame[]) => ({\n  keys: Object.keys(frames[0]).sort(),\n  resumed: frames[0].resumed,\n  resumeFailure: frames[0].resumeFailure,\n  types: frames.map(frame => frame.type),\n});\n\nconst deferredRelease = () => {\n  let release = (): void => undefined;\n  const until = new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    release = resolve;\n  });\n  return {until, release: () => release()};\n};\n\n// Each stored conversation holds one user entry, sent at the given time and reading as its own id.\nconst storeWith = (conversations: Array<[sessionId: string, userId: string, sentAt: string]>): InMemorySessionStore => {\n  const store = new InMemorySessionStore();\n  for (const [sessionId, userId, sentAt] of conversations) {\n    const {entries} = store.create(sessionId, userId);\n    entries.push({role: 'user', content: sessionId, timestamp: sentAt});\n  }\n  return store;\n};\n\n// A store with only the required members, so an optional one can be added, replaced or left out per test.\nconst delegatingTo = (inner: InMemorySessionStore): SessionStore => ({\n  create: (sessionId, userId, options) => inner.create(sessionId, userId, options),\n  get: sessionId => inner.get(sessionId),\n  delete: sessionId => inner.delete(sessionId),\n  count: () => inner.count(),\n  clear: () => inner.clear(),\n});\n\ndescribe('resuming a conversation on reconnect', () => {\n  it('with resume absent, answers a reconnect naming the first id with a new id and no replay', async () => {\n    const {base} = await startEngine(new InMemorySessionStore());\n    const first = await firstTurn(base);\n\n    const frames = await connectAndSettle(`${base}?sessionId=${first}`);\n\n    expect({newId: frames[0].sessionId !== first, shape: shapeOf(frames)}).toEqual({\n      newId: true,\n      shape: {\n        keys: ['examplePrompts', 'message', 'sessionId', 'type'],\n        resumed: undefined,\n        types: ['connected', 'pong'],\n      },\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('with resume on, answers the owner reconnecting with resumed true, entryCount 2 and both stored entries', async () => {\n    const store = new InMemorySessionStore();\n    const {base} = await startEngine(store, RESUME_ON);\n    const first = await firstTurn(base);\n","numLines":200,"startLine":1,"totalLines":592}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_606af483a7cf4ccabe36c9a8","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

socket, which no double can stand in for.\n\nconst servers: Array<{stop: () => Promise<void>}> = [];\nconst clients: WebSocket[] = [];\n\n/** An orchestrator that answers once and stops, which is what commits the turn's assistant entry. */\nexport const answeringOrchestrator: ChatOrchestrator = {\n  processMessage: async () => 'hi',\n  async *processMessageStream(): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n    yield {type: 'text', text: 'hi'};\n    yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\n  },\n};\n\n/** Starts an engine on an ephemeral port and returns the URL a client should open. */\nexport async function startEngine(\n  sessionStore: SessionStore,\n  onDisconnect?: (sessionId: string) => void\n): Promise<string> {\n  const {url} = await startEngineWith({sessionStore, onDisconnect});\n  return url;\n}\n\n/** Starts an engine with whatever a suite overrides, returning the server itself beside the URL a client should open. */\nexport async function startEngineWith(\n  options: Partial<HalServerOptions> & Pick<HalServerOptions, 'sessionStore'>\n): Promise<{url: string; hal: HalServer}> {\n  const hal = createServer({\n    app: (() => undefined) as unknown as Express,\n    wsAuth: async () => ({id: 'u1'}),\n    orchestrator: answeringOrchestrator,\n    ...options,\n  });\n  await hal.start(0);\n  servers.push(hal);\n  const {port} = hal.server.address() as AddressInfo;\n  return {url: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/hal/ws/c1`, hal};\n}\n\n/** Opens a client that the suite's teardown will close, whether its test passed or failed. */\nexport function connectClient(url: string, token = 't'): WebSocket {\n  const client = new WebSocket(url, [HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL, token]);\n  clients.push(client);\n  return client;\n}\n\n/** A promise a test settles by hand, to hold a stream or a hook at a point of its choosing. */\nexport function deferred(): {until: Promise<void>; release: () => void} {\n  let release = (): void => undefined;\n  const until = new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    release = resolve;\n  });\n  return {until, release};\n}\n\n/** Resolves with every frame type seen up to and including the first `until` frame. */\nexport function framesUntil(client: WebSocket, until: string): Promise<string[]> {\n  const seen: string[] = [];\n  return new Promise<string[]>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const {type} = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as {type: string};\n      seen.push(type);\n      if (type === until) resolve(seen);\n    });\n  });\n}\n\n/** Opens a client that asks one question the moment the socket opens, resolving on the first `until` frame. */\nexport function askOnOpen(\n  url: string,\n  {until = 'stream_end', token}: {until?: string; token?: string} = {}\n): {client: WebSocket; finished: Promise<string[]>} {\n  const client = connectClient(url, token);\n  const finished = framesUntil(client, until);\n  client.on('open', () => client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'user_message', content: announcedId(client: WebSocket): () => string {\n  let sessionId = '';\n  client.on('message', raw => {\n    const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as {type: string; sessionId?: string};\n    if (frame.type === 'connected') sessionId = frame.sessionId ?? '';\n  });\n  return () => sessionId;\n}\n\n/** Tears every socket and server down, so a red test reports instead of hanging the run. */\nexport async function stopEngines(): Promise<void> {\n  for (const client of clients.splice(0)) client.terminate();\n  for (const hal of servers.splice(0)) await hal.stop();\n}\n\n/** The one session a store holds, for asserting what survived a close. */\nexport async function onlySession(store: SessionStore, sessionId: string): Promise<ChatSession | undefined> {\n  return (await store.get(sessionId)) as ChatSession | undefined;\n}\n","numLines":110,"startLine":1,"totalLines":110}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_0653a63104bc40f4a80b23de","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

Nothing in the engine calls it yet: the store answers the list, and the route or frame that carries it to a client is still yours to write. `InMemorySessionStore` and `MongoSessionStore` both implement it; a store of your own may leave it out. A summary never carries a conversation's entries or its credentials. Page with `limit` (50 by default, 200 at most, and `0` answers nothing) and `before`, which takes the last summary you saw: the cursor carries both `updatedAt` and `sessionId`, so two conversations saved in the same millisecond cannot straddle a page boundary and go unlisted. See `docs/session-stores.md` § Listing a user's conversations.\n \n ### Changed\ndiff --git a/specs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md b/specs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md\nindex c9ee424..d05eaeb 100644\n--- a/specs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md\n+++ b/specs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md\n@@ -68,3 +68,9 @@ Resume gets a client back into one conversation: the id it names, or the user's\n ## When the store cannot answer\n \n - A store whose collection fails rejects rather than answering a partial or empty list: what to show a user who may have conversations is the caller's decision, and an empty history is not a safe guess ([validated by: rejects rather than answering a partial list when the collection fails](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L225)).\n+\n+## Over the WebSocket protocol\n+\n+- A client sends `{type: 'list_sessions', limit?, before?}` and receives `{type: 'session_list', sessions}` for the socket's authenticated user, with `createdAt` and `updatedAt` serialised as ISO-8601 strings and any client-supplied `userId` ignored ([validated by: answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L93)).\n+- A store without `listFor` answers `{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}`, and a throwing `listFor` logs an error on the `ws` category and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}` ([validated by: answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L134)).\n+- The validator accepts an optional non-negative integer `limit` and an optional `before` cursor whose `sessionId` is 1–128 characters and whose `updatedAt` parses as a valid timestamp, rejecting any other `list_sessions` payload with `INVALID_MESSAGE` without calling `listFor` ([validated by: accepts list_sessions with optional limit and before, strips unknown fields, and rejects malformed '/hal';\n37\t\n38\t  const wss = new WebSocketServer({\n39\t    noServer: true,\n40\t    handleProtocols: selectSubprotocol,\n41\t  });\n42\t\n43\t  const handleMessage = createMessageHandler(options.orchestrator);\n44\t  const examplePrompts = options.toolRegistry?.getExamplePrompts() ?? [];\n45\t\n46\t  const deps = {\n47\t    wsAuth: options.wsAuth,\n48\t    sessionStore: options.sessionStore,\n49\t    handleMessage,\n50\t    basePath,\n51\t    onConnect: options.onConnect,\n52\t    onDisconnect: options.onDisconnect,\n53\t    resume: options.resume,\n54\t  };\n55\t\n56\t  const handleUpgrade = createUpgradeHandler(wss, deps);\n57\t  const handleConnection = createConnectionHandler(deps, examplePrompts);\n58\t\n59\t  const server = http.createServer(options.app);\n60\t\n61\t  server.on('upgrade', (request, socket, head) => {\n62\t    handleUpgrade(request, socket, head);\n63\t  });\n64\t\n65\t  wss.on('connection', ws => {\n66\t    handleConnection(ws as ExtWebSocket);\n67\t  });\n68\t\n69\t  const heartbeatMs = options.heartbeatIntervalMs ?? 30_000;\n70\t\n71\t  const heartbeatInterval = setInterval(() => {\n72\t    wss.clients.forEach(ws => {\n73\t      const extWs = ws as ExtWebSocket;\n74\t      if (!extWs.isAlive) {\n75\t        extWs.terminate();\n76\t        return;\n77\t      }\n78\t      extWs.isAlive = false;\n79\t      extWs.ping();\n80\t    });\n81\t  }, heartbeatMs);\n82\t\n83\t  // The listening socket should hold the process open, not the heartbeat: an engine never started must not.\n84\t  heartbeatInterval.unref();\n85\t\n86\t  wss.on('close', () => clearInterval(heartbeatInterval));\n87\t\n88\t  return {\n89\t    server,\n90\t    wss,\n91\t    start: (port?: number) =>\n92\t      new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {\n93\t        // Refused before the handlers are touched: `listen` throws on a running server, and the swap below stripped its handler.\n94\t        if (server.listening) {\n95\t          reject(new Error('HAL Engine is already started'));\n96\t          return;\n97\t        }\n98\t\n99\t        // ?? not ||, so a configured port 0 means \"let the OS choose\" rather than 8086.\n100\t        const p = port ?? options.port ?? '/hal';\n\n  const wss = new WebSocketServer({\n    noServer: true,\n    handleProtocols: selectSubprotocol,\n  });\n\n  const handleMessage = createMessageHandler(options.orchestrator);\n  const examplePrompts = options.toolRegistry?.getExamplePrompts() ?? {"type":"assistant","message":{"id":"msg_20261031045514685ed053c46447c7","type":"message","role":"assistant","model":"glm-5.3-flash","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"It's jscpd-based with minTokens 50. So any two blocks with ≥50 duplicated tokens get flagged — including within the same file (jscpd scans the whole tree, clones can be same-file). So I must be careful my new `stopEnginesAfterClose` doesn't share ≥50 tokens with the existing `stopEngines`.\n\n`stopEngines` body:\n```ts\nfor (const client of clients.splice(0)) client.terminate();\nfor (const hal of servers.splice(0)) await hal.stop();\n```\nMy new one:\n```ts\nfor (const client of clients.splice(0)) client.terminate();\nfor (const hal of servers.splice(0)) {\n  await eventually(() => hal.wss.clients.size === 0);\n  await hal.stop();\n}\n```\nShared tokens: roughly line 1 (~10 tokens) + partial line 2 (~8 tokens) ≈ 18-20 tokens — well under 50. Safe.\n\nBetter yet — could I avoid a second teardown entirely by making `stopEngines` do the wait? Who uses `stopEngines`? Let me check callers and whether adding a bounded wait could break them (timeouts). Actually adding a wait only SLOWS teardown in the case where clients haven't finished closing... `client.terminate()` is immediate; the server notices quickly (<10-20ms typically). The wait is `eventually(() => wss.clients.size === 0)` — bounded 500ms worst case per server only when a socket lingers. Suites: abandonedOnClose, sessionSurvivesClose, etc. — a few suites, +~10-30ms each. Safe. And it REMOVES a line the suites no longer need... \n\nHmm, but modifying `stopEngines` changes shared behavior beyond the red findings. The red findings require the two suites to share teardown code. If I change `stopEngines` to wait-for-close, then BOTH suites can use the existing `stopEngines` — no second function, no near-duplicate risk, smaller total diff than adding a new function. an absolute path is taken as given\";\n\nconst args = process.argv.slice(2);\nconst flags = args.filter((arg) => arg.startsWith(\"--\"));\nconst docArgs = args.filter((arg) => !arg.startsWith(\"--\"));\n\nconst usageExit = () => {\n  process.stderr.write(`${USAGE}\\n`);\n  process.exit(2);\n};\n\nfor (const flag of flags) {\n  if (flag === \"--json\" || flag === \"--coverage\") {\n    continue;\n  }\n  usageExit();\n}\n\nconst asJson = flags.includes(\"--json\");\nconst asCoverage = flags.includes(\"--coverage\");\n\nconst markdownIn = (dir) =>\n  readdirSync(join(root, dir), { withFileTypes: true })\n    .filter((entry) => entry.isFile() && entry.name.endsWith(\".md\"))\n    .map((entry) => `${dir}/${entry.name}`)\n    .sort();\n\nconst specDocs = () =>\n  readdirSync(join(root, \"specs\"), { withFileTypes: true })\n    .filter((entry) => entry.isDirectory())\n    .map((entry) => `specs/${entry.name}/spec.md`)\n    .sort();\n\nconst discoverDocs = () => [...specDocs(), ...markdownIn(\"adrs\")];","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"201e0564-2c41-4a6d-8255-873a75985435","uuid":"13ec3104-d8e0-4b2e-9dfb-3ef518941aaa","timestamp":"2026-10-30T20:59:41.358Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"// Local counterpart of the ADR half of require-status-matches-coverage:\n// an ADR must declare a lifecycle status the parsers can read, while staying\n// exempt from the coverage tier that rule would also demand of it. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_9f94b97f1ab044fa8b35f824","type":"tool_result","content":"/**\n * require-status-matches-coverage — a spec.md / ADR must declare the lifecycle\n * status its test links can support, and must declare one the parsers can read.\n *\n * Status is the org's backlog signal: the web-UI pills render it, spec-status-upkeep\n * flips it, humans trust it. This rule makes it answerable to the corpus's own\n * `([validated by](test.ts#Lnn))` links rather than to whoever last edited the row:\n *\n *   no testable statement linked    -> Draft\n *   some testable statements linked -> In Progress\n *   every testable statement linked -> Shipped\n *\n * The per-doc complement of `require-statement-links` (which nags per unlinked\n * statement); both read the same `statementCoverage` walk, so the two rules can\n * never disagree about what is linked. Skips `rejected` / `retired` docs via the\n * shared `statusTier`, and docs with no testable statements (no tier to infer).\n *\n * Which folders hold the corpus comes from the `roots` option\n * (`{ spec: [\"specs\"], adr: [\"adrs\"] }` by default) — see `lib/status-coverage.mjs`\n * for the coverage walk.\n *\n * Deliberately carries no `fix`/`suggest`: the `format` CI job runs\n * `eslint --fix` and commits the result back, so a fixer here would silently\n * rewrite spec statuses across the repo on every PR. The message names the label\n * to write; a human writes it.\n */\nimport { statusLabel } from \"./lib/spec-parsers.mjs\";\nimport { DOC_ROOTS_SCHEMA, docKind } from \"./lib/doc-kind.mjs\";\nimport { statusMismatch } from \"./lib/status-coverage.mjs\";\nconst CORPUS = { spec: \"spec\", adr: \"ADR\" };\nconst REQUIREMENT = {\n    spec: \"Add a `| Status | Draft |` row to the header table (one of Draft / In Progress / Shipped / Rejected / Retired).\",\n    adr: \"Add `status: draft` to the YAML frontmatter (one of draft / in progress / shipped / rejected / retired).\",\n};\nfunction mismatchReport(mismatch, kind) {\n    const loc = { line: mismatch.line, column: 1 };\n    if (mismatch.reason === \"untagged\") {\n        return {\n            loc,\n            messageId: \"untagged\",\n            data: { corpus: CORPUS[kind], requirement: REQUIREMENT[kind] },\n        };\n    }\n    return {\n        loc,\n        messageId: \"statusMismatch\",\n        data: {\n            corpus: CORPUS[kind],\n            actual: mismatch.actual,\n            expected: statusLabel(mismatch.expected, kind),\n            linked: mismatch.linked,\n            testable: mismatch.testable,\n        },\n    };\n}\nexport default {\n    meta: {\n        type: \"problem\",\n        docs: {\n            description: \"require every spec.md / ADR to declare a parseable lifecycle status that matches its test-link coverage: no links -> Draft, some -> In Progress, all -> Shipped. Skips rejected/retired docs and docs with no testable statements.\",\n        },\n        schema: [\n            {\n                type: \"object\",\n                properties: { roots: DOC_ROOTS_SCHEMA },\n                additionalProperties: false,\n            },\n        ],\n        messages: {\n            untagged: \"This {{corpus}} declares no status the parsers can read, so its coverage cannot be checked and no status can be rendered for it. {{requirement}}\",\n            statusMismatch: 'Status \"{{actual}}\" does not match this {{corpus}}\\'s test-link coverage — {{linked}} of {{testable}} testable statements carry a ([validated by](test.ts#Lline)) link. Either set the status to \"{{expected}}\", or link the remaining statements to the tests that validate them.',\n        },\n    },\n    create(context) {\n        const kind = docKind(context.filename, context.options[0]?.roots);\n        if (!kind) {\n            return {};\n        }\n        const text = context.sourceCode.getText();\n        return {\n            \"root:exit\"() {\n                const mismatch = statusMismatch(text, kind);\n                if (mismatch) {\n                    context.report(mismatchReport(mismatch, kind));\n                }\n            },\n        };\n    },\n};","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"201e0564-2c41-4a6d-8255-873a75985435","uuid":"20ce12e8-21cf-4008-98ef-807efa4d4bf7","timestamp":"2026-10-30T20:59:57.820Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"/**\n * require-status-matches-coverage — a spec.md / ADR must declare the lifecycle\n * status its test links can support, and must declare one the parsers can read.\n *\n * Status is the org's backlog signal: the web-UI pills render it, spec-status-upkeep\n * flips it, humans trust it. The name is what the\n// author meant, so the name is what the citation records and the line becomes a derived pointer this\n// script repairs. The `#Lnn` stays because the lint rule and the coverage job both index by it, and a\n// citation without one marks the whole file covered rather than one test.\nimport {readFileSync, writeFileSync} from 'node:fs';\nimport {execFileSync} from 'node:child_process';\nimport process from 'node:process';\nimport {dirname, join, normalize} from 'node:path';\nimport {root} from './lib/repo-root.mjs';\n\nconst CITATION = /\\[validated by(?<label>: [^\\]]*)?\\]\\((?<path>(?:\\.\\.\\/)+[\\w./-]+?)#L(?<line>\\d+)\\)/g;\n// Any other href shape is refused rather than ignored: the coverage job resolves `./../x` and `/x`\n// to the same file and counts them, while this gate and the drift check would never have read them.\nconst ANY_HREF = /\\[validated by(?:: [^\\]]*)?\\]\\((?<path>[^)#\\s]+)#L\\d+\\)/g;\n// `xit`, `xdescribe` and `.skip` declare a test that never runs, which validates nothing.\nconst DECLARATION = /^\\s*(?:f?it|f?describe|test)\\(\\s*(['\"`])((?:\\\\.|(?!\\1).)*)\\1/;\nconst SKIPPED = /^\\s*(?:x(?:it|describe|test)|(?:it|describe|test)\\.skip)\\(\\s*(['\"`])((?:\\\\.|(?!\\1).)*)\\1/;\nconst TEST_FILE = /\\.(?:test|spec)\\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/;\n\nconst cache = new Map();\nconst args = process.argv.slice(2);\nconst fix = args.includes('--fix');\nconst named = args.filter(arg => !arg.startsWith('--'));\nconst findings = [];\nlet checked = 0;\nlet repaired = 0;\n\nfor (const spec of named.length > 0 ? {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_e4393b5e9e924070b4870864","type":"tool_result","content":"ci.yml\nguard-main-pushes.yml\nlore-ingest.yml\nlore-trace-impact.yml\npublish.yml\nname: CI\n\non:\n  pull_request:\n  push:\n    branches: [main]\n  # Manual runs: re-checking a branch against a moved main, or confirming a gate after\n  # changing one, without pushing an empty commit.\n  workflow_dispatch:\n  # An advisory published after a merge is invisible until someone opens a pull request, and this\n  # repository can go days without one. Monday 07:00 UTC; only `build-chain` answers it.\n  schedule:\n    - cron: '0 7 * * 1'\n\n# Every job here only reads the checkout; the repo default is write.\npermissions:\n  contents: read\n\n# A newer push to the same branch supersedes an in-flight run. main is exempt:\n# every commit there should have its own recorded result.\nconcurrency:\n  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}\n  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}\n\njobs:\n  verify:\n    name: Verify\n    # The scheduled run exists for the dependency audit; re-running the suite on an unchanged\n    # tree every Monday would report nothing new.\n    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n          # Full history, not for this job but for the spec anchor check below:\n          # it resolves cited content from\n          # origin/main, which a shallow clone cannot serve.\n          fetch-depth: 0\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      # --ignore-scripts so `prepare` does not build on install: what a lifecycle script\n      # runs is out of this workflow's control, and the Build step below is where a broken\n      # compile should be reported. Type check catches it earlier still.\n      - name: Install\n        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n\n      # Every `npm run` step below is one link of the `verify` script in\n      # package.json, in the same order - scripts/verify-script.test.ts holds\n      # the two together - and kept as separate steps so a red run names the\n      # gate that failed rather than a single opaque command.\n      - name: Type check\n        run: npm run typecheck\n\n      # example/ is outside tsconfig.json's rootDir, so nothing checked the one\n      # file the README and the guide are written against.\n      - name: Type check the example\n        run: npm run typecheck:example\n\n      - name: Lint (--max-warnings 0)\n        run: npm run eslint\n\n      # Reports, never blocks. The one rule it runs is `warn`, so the step exits\n      # 0 on its own and carries no continue-on-error: a non-zero exit here now\n      # means the config itself broke, and that should fail. Its findings render\n      # as warning annotations rather than failures, which is what a report on a\n      # passing check should look like.\n      #\n      # require-statement-links counts spec statements with no test behind them.\n      # Most of what it reports needs a test written rather than a line changed,\n      # so the count is meant to be visible on every run and to fall over time.\n      # Its test-side mirror, require-spec-link, is satisfied and gates in the\n      # Lint step above. Never add a rule here to escape a red gate -\n      # eslint.config.backlog.mjs says what belongs.\n      - name: Spec traceability backlog (report)\n        run: npm run lint:backlog\n\n      - name: Format check\n        run: npm run prettier:check\n\n      # Runs the whole suite and fails it on the committed coverage floor in\n      # jest.config.js, so this is the test gate rather than an extra pass.\n      - name: Test (with coverage floor)\n        run: npm run test:coverage\n\n      - name: Build\n        run: npm run build\n\n      # Anchors drift silently: a cited file gaining or losing lines above the\n      # cited one leaves the link pointing at different content, and the spec\n      # still reads as cited. Resolves content at origin/main, which the\n      # fetch-depth: 0 above exists to provide. A red check is fixed by running\n      # `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs` and committing the result.\n      - name: Spec anchor check\n        run: node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs --check origin/main\n\n      # A citation counts as coverage only in its statement's trailing\n      # parenthetical; one written mid-statement is dropped by the Lore job in silence,\n      # so the spec reads as cited while its coverage is zero. Monday 07:00 UTC; only `build-chain` answers it.\n  schedule:\n    - cron: '0 7 * * 1'\n\n# Every job here only reads the checkout; the repo default is write.\npermissions:\n  contents: read\n\n# A newer push to the same branch supersedes an in-flight run. main is exempt:\n# every commit there should have its own recorded result.\nconcurrency:\n  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}\n  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}\n\njobs:\n  verify:\n    name: Verify\n    # The scheduled run exists for the dependency audit; re-running the suite on an unchanged\n    # tree every Monday would report nothing new.\n    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n          # Full history, not for this job but for the spec anchor check below:\n          # it resolves cited content from\n          # origin/main, which a shallow clone cannot serve.\n          fetch-depth: 0\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      # --ignore-scripts so `prepare` does not build on install: what a lifecycle script\n      # runs is out of this workflow's control, and the Build step below is where a broken\n      # compile should be reported. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_1530b9255d4b4b40bb55bbf4","type":"tool_result","content":"#!/usr/bin/env node\n// Re-points specs' [validated by](../../src/X.test.ts#Lnn) anchors after\n// edits to the cited file - any cited\n// repository file, whatever its kind: each anchor's line number is\n// resolved to the content it cited in the base ref's copy of that file,\n// that content is found in the working copy (compared with quotes and\n// whitespace dropped, so a formatter pass is not drift), and the anchor is\n// rewritten to the match whose surrounding lines agree with the baseline's. When the cited\n// content occurs on several working lines, each candidate is scored by how\n// many of the baseline's neighbouring lines it reproduces at the same offsets;\n// a candidate whose context uniquely wins is chosen, and a tie is reported as\n// ambiguous for manual fix (exit 1 in both modes) instead of guessing. An\n// anchor into a file built of repeated blocks - a workflow whose jobs share an\n// identical setup - must therefore cite a line unique to its own step, because\n// the resolver refuses to guess between indistinguishable candidates.\n//\n// Usage:\n//   node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs [--check] [base-ref]\n//\n// base-ref defaults to origin/main and must be the baseline the anchors were\n// last correct against. Baseline line numbers are read from the base ref's\n// copy of each spec, never from the working copy, so re-running against the\n// same baseline is a no-op instead of a second translation. A spec whose\n// anchor set (the ordered list of test paths it cites) differs from the base\n// ref is skipped whole: its anchors were authored against the working tree,\n// and no baseline exists to repoint them from. An individual anchor whose\n// line number differs from the base spec's at the same position was\n// deliberately retargeted by a spec edit: it is accepted as authored, never\n// rewritten, and reported as \"retargeted (not checked)\".\n//\n// Independent of any baseline, every anchor must land on a line that exists\n// and carries content: an anchor whose target file is missing, whose line is\n// beyond the end of the file, or whose line is blank or closing punctuation\n// is reported as rotten and fails the run in both modes. An anchor\n// into a test file must additionally land on the it/test/describe declaration\n// itself, because a line inside a test body names no case a reader can check.\n// Non-test targets - a workflow, a config, package.json - are exempt from that\n// last check: they have no declaration to land on.\n//\n// Also independent of any baseline, a short-form [Lnnn](...#Lmmm) label must\n// name the line its own href points at. Labels are re-synced to their href\n// after the anchor rewrite, so a repointed href carries its label with it;\n// --check reports label/href disagreement as mislabelled and fails.\n// --check rewrites nothing, so it judges each label against its current\n// (un-repointed) href: a stale href is reported as stale, and once a plain run\n// repoints it the label follows, so the two runs still converge in one pass.\n//\n// --check rewrites nothing and exits 1 when any anchor is stale (its baseline\n// content now lives on a different line), unresolved (that content no\n// longer exists), rotten, or mislabelled. Without --check, stale anchors are\n// rewritten in place, labels are synced, and unresolved or rotten ones are\n// reported for manual fix with exit 1; a rotten anchor the rewrite itself\n// repoints needs no manual fix and is not reported.\n\nimport { execFileSync } from \"node:child_process\";\nimport { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\nimport { dirname, join, normalize } from \"node:path\";\nimport process from \"node:process\";\nimport { splitArgs } from \"./lib/cli-args.mjs\";\n\nconst TRACKED_PATH = String.raw`(?:\\.\\.\\/)+(?:scripts\\/[\\w./-]+|[\\w./-]+\\.[A-Za-z]+)`;\nconst ANCHOR = new RegExp(String.raw`(${TRACKED_PATH})#L(\\d+)`, \"g\");\n\n// A short-form [Lnnn](../../src/X.test.ts#Lmmm) link: its visible label is a\n// bare line number that must equal the href's #L number. The label has no\n// meaning apart from the href, so it is force-synced to the href even when the\n// href was manually retargeted; descriptive labels ([validated by], ...) never\n// match and are never touched.\nconst LABEL_LINK = new RegExp(String.raw`\\[L(\\d+)\\]\\((${TRACKED_PATH})#L(\\d+)\\)`, \"g\");\n\nconst { flags, positional } = splitArgs(process.argv.slice(2));\n\nif (flags.some((flag) => flag !== \"--check\") || positional.length > 1) {\n  process.stderr.write(\"usage: repoint-spec-anchors.mjs [--check] [base-ref]\\n\");\n  process.exit(2);\n}\nconst checkMode = flags.includes(\"--check\");\nconst baseRef = positional[0] ?? \"origin/main\";\n\nconst root = process.cwd();","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"201e0564-2c41-4a6d-8255-873a75985435","uuid":"8cc23c21-f297-4c55-986e-7deabf78ff40","timestamp":"2026-10-30T21:00:49.529Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"#!/usr/bin/env node\n// Re-points specs' [validated by](../../src/X.test.ts#Lnn) anchors after\n// edits to the cited file - any cited\n// repository file, whatever its kind: each anchor's line number is\n// resolved to the content it cited in the base ref's copy of that file,\n// that content is found in the working copy (compared with quotes and\n// whitespace dropped, so a formatter pass is not drift), and the anchor is\n// rewritten to the match whose surrounding lines agree with the baseline's. 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\n  },\n};\n\nconst servers: Array<ReturnType<typeof createServer>> = [];\nconst clients: WebSocket[] = [];\n\nconst eventually = async (check: () => boolean): Promise<void> => {\n  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 50 && !check(); attempt++) await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 10));\n};\n\n// Silenced for the whole file: the server logs every undefined});\n});\n\nafterAll(() => {\n  setLogger();\n});\n\n// Each server sees its sockets close before it stops, so no close is logged after the logger above is restored.\nafterEach(async () => {\n  for (const client of clients.splice(0)) client.terminate();\n  for (const hal of servers.splice(0)) {\n    const {wss} = hal;\n    await eventually(() => wss.clients.size === 0);\n    await hal.stop();\n  }\n});\n\n// The authenticated user is read per upgrade, so one test can reconnect as someone else.\nconst startEngine = async (\n  store: SessionStore,\n  resume?: orchestrator,\n    resume,\n    onConnect: (session, {resumed}) => void connects.push({sessionId: session.sessionId, resumed}),\n    onDisconnect: sessionId => void disconnected.push(sessionId),\n  });\n  // Resolves once the server itself has seen its first socket close, which the client's own close can precede.\n  const firstServerClose = new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    hal.wss.once('connection', socket => socket.once('close', () => resolve()));\n  });\n  await hal.start(0);\n  servers.push(hal);\n  const {port} = hal.server.address() as AddressInfo;\n  return {auth, (base: string): Promise<string> => {\n  const client = open(base);\n  let sessionId = '';\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = client.close();\n  await once(client, 'close');\n  return sessionId;\n};\n\n// A ping sent on connect is a barrier: its pong can only follow every frame the replay wrote.\nconst connectAndSettle = async (url: string, token?: string): Promise<Frame[]> => {\n  const client = open(url, token);\n  const frames: Frame[] = [];\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      frames.push(frame);\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1}));\n      if (frame.type === 'pong') resolve();\n    });\n  });\n  return frames;\n};\n\nconst upserts = (frames: Frame[]) =>\n  frames.filter(frame => frame.type === 'entry_upsert').map(({index, entry}) => ({index, entry}));\n\nconst shapeOf = (frames: Frame[]) => ({\n  keys: Object.keys(frames[0]).sort(),\n  resumed: frames[0].resumed,\n  resumeFailure: frames[0].resumeFailure,\n  types: return {until, release: () => release()};\n};\n\n// Each stored conversation holds one user entry, sent at the given time and reading as its own id.\nconst storeWith = (conversations: const {entries} = store.create(sessionId, userId);\n    entries.push({role: 'user', content: sessionId, timestamp: sentAt});\n  }\n  return store;\n};\n\n// A store with only the required members, so announced.\nconst firstTurn = async (base: string): Promise<string> => {\n  const client = open(base);\n  let sessionId = '';\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') sessionId = frame.sessionId ?? '';\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'user_message', content: 'hello'}));\n      if (frame.type === 'stream_end') resolve();\n    });\n  });\n  client.close();\n  await once(client, 'close');\n  return sessionId;\n};\n\n// A ping sent on connect is a barrier: its pong can only follow every frame the replay wrote.\nconst connectAndSettle = async (url: string, token?: string): Promise<Frame[]> => {\n  const client = open(url, token);\n  const frames: Frame[] = [];\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      frames.push(frame);\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1}));\n      if (frame.type === 'pong') resolve();\n    });\n  });\n  return frames;\n};\n\nconst upserts = (frames: Frame[]) =>\n  frames.filter(frame => frame.type === 'entry_upsert').map(({index, entry}) => ({index, entry}));\n\nconst shapeOf = (frames: Frame[]) => ({\n  keys: Object.keys(frames[0]).sort(),\n  resumed: frames[0].resumed,\n  resumeFailure: frames[0].resumeFailure,\n  types: frames.map(frame => frame.type),\n});\n\nconst deferredRelease = () => {\n  let release = (): void => undefined;\n  const until = new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    release = resolve;\n  });\n  return {until, release: () => release()};\n};\n\n// Each stored conversation holds one user entry, sent at the given time and reading as its own id.\nconst storeWith = (conversations: Array<[sessionId: string, userId: string, sentAt: string]>): InMemorySessionStore => {\n  const store = new InMemorySessionStore();\n  for (const [sessionId, userId, sentAt] of conversations) {\n    const {entries} = store.create(sessionId, userId);\n    entries.push({role: 'user', content: sessionId, timestamp: sentAt});\n  }\n  return store;\n};\n\n// A store with only the required members, so an optional one can be added, replaced or left out per test.\nconst delegatingTo = (inner: InMemorySessionStore): SessionStore => ({\n  create: (sessionId, userId, options) => inner.create(sessionId, 'node:events';\nimport type {WebSocket} from 'ws';\nimport type {SessionResumeOptions} from './ws/sessionResume.js';\nimport {answeringOrchestrator, connectClient, delegatingTo, eventually, startEngineWith, stopEngines} from './wsTestSupport.js';\nimport {InMemorySessionStore} from '../infrastructure/stores/inMemorySessionStore.js';\nimport type {ChatOrchestrator} from '../orchestration/chatOrchestrator.js';\nimport type {MessageChunk} from '../types/ai.js';\nimport type {ConnectedMessage} from '../types/messages.js';\nimport type {SessionEntry} from '../types/session.js';\nimport type {SessionStore} from '../types/sessionStore.js';\nimport {setLogger} from '../shared/logger.js';\n\n// Real upgrades over a real socket: what a reconnect is sent is the contract, and no double can observe it.\n\ninterface Frame {\n  type: string;\n  sessionId?: string;\n  resumed?: boolean;\n  entryCount?: number;\n  resumeFailure?: string;\n  index?: number;\n  entry?: SessionEntry;\n}\n\nconst NEVER_ISSUED = '0f1e2d3c-4b5a-4968-8776-655443322110';\nconst RESUME_ON: SessionResumeOptions = {enabled: true};\nconst LATEST_ON: SessionResumeOptions = {enabled: true, latest: true};\nconst HALF_ANSWER: SessionEntry = {\n  role: 'assistant',\n  content: 'half',\n  timestamp: '2026-09-30T08:00:01.000Z',\n  isStreaming: true,\n};\n\n// A tool's suppression lands while the answer is still open, as when a provider ends a tool round with no stop.\nconst suppressingMidAnswer: ChatOrchestrator = {\n  processMessage: async () => 'before after',\n  async *processMessageStream(): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n    yield {type: 'text', text: 'before'};\n    yield {type: 'suppress_output'} as unknown as MessageChunk;\n    yield {type: 'text', text: ' after'};\n    yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\n  },\n};\n\n// Silenced for the whole file: the server logs every connection and close, and these tests read frames, not logs.\nbeforeAll(() => {\n  setLogger({debug: () => undefined, info: () => undefined, warn: () => undefined, error: () => undefined});\n});\n\nafterAll(() => {\n  setLogger();\n});\n\n// The shared teardown waits for each server to see its sockets close, so no close is logged after the logger above is restored.\nafterEach(async () => {\n  await stopEngines();\n});\n\n// The authenticated user is read per upgrade, so one test can reconnect as someone else.\nconst startEngine = async (\n  store: SessionStore,\n  resume?: SessionResumeOptions,\n  orchestrator: ChatOrchestrator = answeringOrchestrator\n) => {\n  const auth = {userId: 'u1'};\n  const connects: Array<{sessionId: string; resumed: boolean}> = [];\n  const disconnected: string[] = [];\n  const {url: base, hal} = await startEngineWith({\n    sessionStore: store,\n    orchestrator,\n    resume,\n    wsAuth: async () => ({id: auth.userId}),\n    onConnect: (session, {resumed}) => void connects.push({sessionId: session.sessionId, resumed}),\n    onDisconnect: sessionId => void disconnected.push(sessionId),\n  });\n  // Registered before the test opens its first socket, which only the returned URL can start.\n  const firstServerClose = new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    hal.wss.once('connection', socket => socket.once('close', () => resolve()));\n  });\n  return {auth, connects, disconnected, firstServerClose, base};\n};\n\nconst open = (url: string, token = 't'): WebSocket => connectClient(url, token);\n\n// One question answered and the socket closed, returning the id the connected frame announced.\nconst firstTurn = async (base: string): Promise<string> => {\n  const client = open(base);\n  let sessionId = '';\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') sessionId = frame.sessionId ?? '';\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'user_message', content: 'hello'}));\n      if (frame.type === 'stream_end') resolve();\n    });\n  });\n  client.close();\n  await once(client, 'close');\n  return sessionId;\n};\n\n// A ping sent on connect is a barrier: its pong can only follow every frame the replay wrote.\nconst connectAndSettle = async (url: string, token?: string): Promise<Frame[]> => {\n  const client = open(url, token);\n  const frames: Frame[] = [];\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      frames.push(frame);\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1}));\n      if (frame.type === 'pong') resolve();\n    });\n  });\n  return frames;\n};\n\nconst upserts = (frames: Frame[]) =>\n  frames.filter(frame => frame.type === 'entry_upsert').map(({index, entry}) => ({index, entry}));\n\nconst shapeOf = (frames: Frame[]) => ({\n  keys: Object.keys(frames[0]).sort(),\n  resumed: frames[0].resumed,\n  resumeFailure: frames[0].resumeFailure,\n  types: frames.map(frame => frame.type),\n});\n\nconst deferredRelease = () => {\n  let release = (): void => undefined;\n  const until = new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    release = resolve;\n  });\n  return {until, release: () => release()};\n};\n\n// Each stored conversation holds one user entry, sent at the given time and reading as its own id.\nconst storeWith = (conversations: Array<[sessionId: string, userId: string, sentAt: string]>): InMemorySessionStore => {\n  const store = new InMemorySessionStore();\n  for (const [sessionId, userId, sentAt] of conversations) {\n    const {entries} = store.create(sessionId, userId);\n    entries.push({role: 'user', content: sessionId, timestamp: sentAt});\n  }\n  return store;\n};\n\n// A store with only the required members, so an optional one can be added, replaced or left out per test.\nconst delegatingTo = (inner: InMemorySessionStore): SessionStore => ({\n  create: (sessionId, userId, options) => inner.create(sessionId, userId, options),\n  get: sessionId => inner.get(sessionId),\n  delete: sessionId => inner.delete(sessionId),\n  count: () => inner.count(),\n  clear: () => inner.clear(),\n});\n\ndescribe('resuming a conversation on reconnect', () => {\n  it('with resume absent, answers a reconnect naming the first id with a new id and no replay', async () => {\n    const {base} = await startEngine(new InMemorySessionStore());\n    const first = await firstTurn(base);\n\n    const frames = await connectAndSettle(`${base}?sessionId=${first}`);\n\n    expect({newId: frames[0].sessionId !== first, shape: shapeOf(frames)}).toEqual({\n      newId: true,\n      shape: {\n        keys: ['examplePrompts', 'message', 'sessionId', 'type'],\n        resumed: undefined,\n        types: ['connected', 'pong'],\n      },\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('with resume on, answers the owner reconnecting with resumed true, entryCount 2 and both stored entries', async () => {\n    const store = new InMemorySessionStore();\n    const {base} = await startEngine(store, RESUME_ON);\n    const first = await firstTurn(base);\n\n    const frames = await connectAndSettle(`${base}?sessionId=${first}`);\n\n    const stored = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify((await store.get(first))?.entries)) as SessionEntry[];\n    expect({connected: frames[0], replay: upserts(frames)}).toMatchObject({\n      connected: {type: 'connected', sessionId: first, resumed: true, entryCount: 2},\n      replay: [\n        {index: 0, entry: stored[0]},\n        {index: 1, entry: stored[1]},\n      ],\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('answers another user naming the id exactly as it answers an id that was never issued', async () => {\n    const {auth, base} = await startEngine(new InMemorySessionStore(), RESUME_ON);\n    const first = await firstTurn(base);\n    auth.userId = 'u2';\n\n    const otherUser = await connectAndSettle(`${base}?sessionId=${first}`);\n    const neverIssued = await connectAndSettle(`${base}?sessionId=${NEVER_ISSUED}`);\n\n    expect({fresh: otherUser[0].sessionId !== first, otherUser: shapeOf(otherUser)}).toEqual({\n      fresh: true,\n      otherUser: shapeOf(neverIssued),\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('answers a never-issued id with resumed false, resumeFailure unknown, and no replay or error', async () => {\n    const {base} = await startEngine(new InMemorySessionStore(), RESUME_ON);\n\n    const frames = await connectAndSettle(`${base}?sessionId=${NEVER_ISSUED}`);\n\n    expect(shapeOf(frames)).toEqual({\n      keys: ['examplePrompts', 'message', 'resumeFailure', 'resumed', 'sessionId', 'type'],\n      resumed: false,\n      resumeFailure: 'unknown',\n      types: ['connected', 'pong'],\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('never adopts a requested id as a key: one session, under the id the server minted', async () => {\n    const store = new InMemorySessionStore();\n    const {base} = await startEngine(store, RESUME_ON);\n\n    const frames = await connectAndSettle(`${base}?sessionId=${NEVER_ISSUED}`);\n\n    expect({\n      held: await store.count(),\n      adopted: (await store.get(NEVER_ISSUED)) !== '../wsTestSupport.js';\n\n// The frames, in order, are the contract - above all for suppression, which retracts.\n\n// One line per frame; entries carry generated timestamps no assertion should read.\nconst wire = (sent: OutgoingMessage[]): string[] =>\n  sent.map(frame => {\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_upsert') {\n      const content = 'content' in frame.entry ? frame.entry.content : '';\n      return `upsert ${frame.index} ${frame.entry.role} ${JSON.stringify(content)}`;\n    }\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_delta') return `delta ${frame.index} ${JSON.stringify(frame.delta)}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_commit') return `commit ${frame.index}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_skip') return `skip ${frame.index}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'error') return `error ${frame.code}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'pong') return `pong ${frame.timestamp}`;\n    return frame.type;\n  });\n\nconst text = (value: string): MessageChunk => ({type: 'text', text: value});\nconst STOP: MessageChunk = {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\nconst SUPPRESS = {type: 'suppress_output'} as unknown as MessageChunk;\n\ninterface StreamScript {\n  failWith?: Error;\n  pauseAfter?: {chunks: number; until: Promise<void>};\n}\n\nconst harness = (chunks: MessageChunk[], {failWith, pauseAfter}: StreamScript = {}) => {\n  const sent: OutgoingMessage[] = [];\n  const ws = {send: (raw: string) => sent.push(JSON.parse(raw) as OutgoingMessage)} as unknown as WebSocket;\n\n  const stream = async function* (): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n    for (const [position, chunk] of chunks.entries()) {\n      if (pauseAfter && position === pauseAfter.chunks) await pauseAfter.until;\n      yield chunk;\n    }\n    if (failWith) throw failWith;\n  };\n\n  const processMessageStream = jest.fn(stream);\n  const orchestrator = {processMessageStream} as unknown as ChatOrchestrator;\n  const session: ChatSession = {sessionId: 's1', userId: 'u1', entries: []};\n\n  const handle = createMessageHandler(orchestrator);\n\n  return {\n    session,\n    processMessageStream,\n    sent,\n    frames: () => wire(sent),\n    send: (raw: unknown = {type: 'user_message', content: 'hello'}, signal?: AbortSignal) =>\n      handle(ws, session, raw, signal),\n  };\n};\n\ndescribe('the websocket message handler', () => {\n  describe('dispatch', () => {\n    it('rejects an unparseable message and never starts a stream', async () => {\n      const h = harness([]);\n\n      await h.send({type: 'nonsense'});\n\n      const {calls} = h.processMessageStream.mock;\n\n      expect({frames: h.frames(), streams: calls.length}).toEqual({frames: ['error INVALID_MESSAGE'], streams: 0});\n    });\n\n    it('answers a ping with the timestamp it was given', async () => {\n      const h = harness([]);\n\n      await h.send({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1234});\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual(['pong 1234']);\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe('a plain assistant reply', () => {\n    it('sends the user entry, then the assistant entry, its delta, its commit and stream_end', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('hi there'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual([\n        'upsert 0 user \"hello\"',\n        'upsert 1 assistant \"\"',\n        'delta 1 \"hi there\"',\n        'commit 1',\n        'stream_end',\n      ]);\n    });\n\n    it('leaves the committed assistant entry in the session, no longer streaming', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('hi there'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      const {entries} = h.session;\n\n      expect(entries[1]).toMatchObject({role: 'assistant', content: 'hi there', isStreaming: false});\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe('thinking segments', () => {\n    it('commits the thinking entry before the assistant entry opens', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('<thinking>pondering</thinking>answer'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual([\n        'upsert 0 user \"hello\"',\n        'upsert 1 thinking \"\"',\n        'delta 1 \"pondering\"',\n        'commit 1',\n        'upsert 2 assistant \"\"',\n        'delta 2 \"answer\"',\n        'commit 2',\n        'stream_end',\n      ]);\n    });\n\n    it('commits the thinking entry when text resumes, not when a tool entry appears', async () => {\n      const h = harness([\n        text('<thinking>I should look up the weather for Berlin.</thinking>'),\n        {type: 'tool_use', toolCall: {id: 'c1', name: 'get_weather', input: {location: 'Berlin'}}} as MessageChunk,\n        text('Berlin currently has '),\n        text('a temperature of 18 degrees Celsius with clear skies.'),\n        STOP,\n      ]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual([\n        'upsert 0 user \"hello\"',\n        'upsert 1 thinking \"\"',\n        'delta 1 \"I should look up the weather for Berlin.\"',\n        'upsert 2 tool \"\"',\n        'commit 1',\n        'upsert 3 assistant \"\"',\n        'delta 3 \"Berlin currently has \"',\n        'delta 3 \"a temperature of 18 degrees Celsius with clear skies.\"',\n        'commit 3',\n        'stream_end',\n      ]);\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe('tool chunks', () => {\n    it('sends a tool entry for a tool call', async () => {\n      const h = harness([{type: 'tool_use', toolCall: {id: 'c1', name: 'lookup', input: {q: 1}}}, STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual(['upsert 0 user \"hello\"', 'upsert 1 tool \"\"', 'stream_end']);\n    });\n\n    it('forwards a tool result to the client untouched', async () => {\n      const forwarded = {type: 'entry_commit', index: 41} as OutgoingMessage;\n      const h = harness([{type: 'tool_result', clientMessages: [forwarded]} as MessageChunk, STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual(['upsert 0 user \"hello\"', 'commit 41', 'stream_end']);\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe('suppression', () => {\n    it('blanks an assistant entry that was already sent', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('leaked'), STOP, SUPPRESS]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual([\n        'upsert 0 user \"hello\"',\n        'upsert 1 assistant \"\"',\n        'delta 1 \"leaked\"',\n        'commit 1',\n        'upsert 1 assistant \"\"',\n await h.send();\n\n      const {entries} = h.session;\n\n      expect(entries[1]).toMatchObject({role: 'assistant', content: 'hidden', isStreaming: false});\n    });\n\n    it('does not resurrect an const [, answer, after] = h.session.entries;\n      expect({frames: h.frames(), answer, after}).toMatchObject({\n        frames: [\n          'upsert 0 user \"hello\"',\n          'upsert 1 assistant
